rows.why: Blueprint shows lapels whose points project upward and outward past the gorge plus a distinct rectangular collar band across the neck. The live photo, at 3.5x zoom on both sides, shows an open V-wedge between collar leaf and lapel with the lapel tip angled downward - an unambiguous NOTCH lapel - and no collar band anywhere, so it depicts the sibling option Notch with/without Collar Band, not a peak.

Blueprint is an interior cutaway with a shaped chest piece over a base interlining and a taped front edge; the live photo shows dense rows of hand pad-stitching over at least two distinct tan interlining layers, which is the signature of hand-canvassed construction and the opposite of a single fused layer. It is also not separable from the shipped Full Canvas and Fused Canvas photos, which show the same pad-stitched cutaway language.

Blueprint is a plain vest front with no chest pocket drawn. The live photo frames both chest panels from shoulder to waist at large scale under directional light, both chest areas are unbroken navy cloth, and the two lower welts visible at the bottom of frame act as a control proving a welt at that lighting would have broken the plane - the absence is positively demonstrated, not merely cropped away.

Blueprint draws a single chest welt on the wearer's left with a red stripe along the pocket seam and a pale stripe along its bottom edge; the live photo shows that same left-chest welt as a two-tone band - red on the seam half, white on the bottom half - so both named zones are separately readable and it is clearly distinct from the DIY Seam (seam only) sibling.

Blueprint puts a narrow red edging strip along the outer edge of both lapels, the collar and the front edge; the live photo shows an ivory tape running exactly those edges, so the named feature is correct and cannot be confused with the full-contrast-lapel sibling. Noted deviation: the photo also adds the same tape to both armholes, the hem and all three pocket welts, which the drawing does not show and which trespasses on the separate contrast-pocket-vest field.

Blueprint marks one red buttonhole on each of the two lapels; the live photo shows exactly two red-stitched buttonholes, one per lapel, and a zoom on the wearer's-right one confirms both bar-tack ends are inside the frame, so the count of 2 and the both-sides pairing are legible.

Blueprint shows the vest interior with a red piping line along the junction of the front facing and the lining; the live photo shows the garment open on a hanger with bright red corded piping running that exact facing/lining seam from shoulder to hem, and a zoom on the mid-body confirms a finished sleeveless armhole, so it is a vest interior and not a jacket.

Blueprint marks six buttons in two columns of three on a wrapped double-breasted front; a brightened zoom confirms six buttons as two columns of three, with stitched buttonholes beside the middle and bottom buttons of the closing column and none at the top row, i.e. two of six fastening, which separates 6x2 from the 6x3 sibling. Noted deviation: hem is straight in the drawing but pointed in the photo.

Blueprint marks three button positions in a single centre column on a single-breasted front; the live photo shows exactly three buttons in one column, all fastened, on a navy V-neck waistcoat with two lower besoms and a pointed hem - the count of 3 is unambiguous and separates it from the sb-4/5/6 siblings.

Blueprint shows a collarless, lapel-less neckline with two straight edges converging to a sharp point above the top button; the live photo shows exactly that - a deep straight-sided V terminating in a crisp apex just above the top button, with no collar band and no lapel - so it cannot be mistaken for the U-neckline or any lapel sibling.

Blueprint shows the hem running level across the whole front with no point; the live photo has the entire hem in frame running essentially horizontally with square front corners and no V, clearly distinct from the Regular/Small Point/Slant siblings and from the Round option's curved corners.

Blueprint shows two chest besoms drawn in red, one on each front panel, symmetrically placed. The live photo is a tight three-quarter crop containing only ONE besom, on the wearer's left chest; a brightened zoom of the left edge confirms the wearer's right panel carries no welt and its pocket zone is cut off by the frame. One besom instead of two reads identically to the Left Besom sibling that also exists in this menu.

Blueprint shows the lower pocket as a besom mouth with a rectangular flap hanging over it; the live photo shows a horizontal slit pocket covered by a flap (no patch outline, no slant), separating it from the Besom no-flap, Patch and Slant Besom with Flap siblings. Noted deviations: flap corners are rounded where the drawing squares them, and as in the drawing the besom itself is hidden beneath the flap so besom-vs-welt cannot be verified.
